prompt: A set contains exactly the numbers 1 and 2. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: The empty set is a subset of it.
options.explanation: There is no element of the empty set that could fail the subset test.

options.text: The empty set is one of its elements.
options.explanation: The only listed elements are the numbers 1 and 2.

options.text: A different set containing only the empty set has one element.
options.explanation: Its one element is itself a set; the outer collection is not empty.

options.text: Listing 2, 1 and 1 describes the same set.
options.explanation: Sets ignore order and duplicate listings.

options.text: The set containing only 1 is one of its elements.
options.explanation: That singleton is a subset, but it is not one of the two number elements.

workedExample: First ask what the elements are: here they are numbers. Membership checks one object against that list. Subset inclusion instead checks every element of a collection. The empty collection has no counterexample to that check. Wrapping it in an outer set creates a collection with one element. Reordering or repeating listed elements never changes membership.
